newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Taleban foreign minister, commander said arrested.
newsitem.headline: Taleban foreign minister, commander said arrested.

text.p: Opposition forces have arrested Afghanistan's Taleban government Foreign Minister Mullah Mohammad Ghous and its northern military commander Mullah Abdul Razzaq, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said on Wednesday.

The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted a spokesman for the opposition Hezb-i-Wahdat faction as saying the two men had been arrested in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, where fierce fighting had forced the Taleban to retreat on Wednesday.

AIP said it was not known when the arrests took place but Taleban sources in the southern city of Kandahar, headquarters of the purist Islamic militia, had wireless contact with their fighters in Mazar-i-Sharif until 9.30 a.m. (0500 GMT) on Wednesday.

It quoted a Wahdat spokesman in Pakistan's northwestern town of Peshawar, Mohammad Abbas Diljoo, as saying thousands of Taleban fighters were arrested and several hundred killed in the 15-hour battle with Wahdat and ethnic Uzbek troops of General Abdul Malik. But there was no independent confirmation of this.

A Reuters correspondent in Mazar-i-Sharif reported earlier it was clear that the black-turbaned Taleban in the city, whose total number was at least 3,000, had suffered a total defeat at the hands of Malik's forces and Hezb-i-Wahdat fighters.
